schema: Each reel: say = spoken text for ElevenLabs (acronyms spelled as spaced letters, '...' for pauses, never say 'ISC2'); show = on-screen caption; card = big centre text; card_style = default|myth|fact|answer|formula; quiz = optional multiple choice, revealed at quiz.reveal (segment index, 0-based). Post copy never uses the word 'lecture'.

reels.topic: Code of ethics: the four canons
reels.hook: Your boss says: hide the flaw.

segments.say: Your boss asks you to hide a known safety flaw from customers. What does a C I S S P do?
segments.show: Your boss asks you to hide a known safety flaw from customers. What does a CISSP do?

segments.say: The code of ethics has four canons... in priority order.
segments.show: The code of ethics has four canons, in priority order.

segments.say: One. Protect society, the common good, public trust, and the infrastructure.
segments.show: 1. Protect society, the common good, public trust and the infrastructure.

segments.say: Two. Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, and legally.
segments.show: 2. Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally.

segments.say: Three. Provide diligent and competent service to principals... that's your employer.
segments.show: 3. Provide diligent and competent service to principals (your employer).

segments.say: Four. Advance and protect the profession.
segments.show: 4. Advance and protect the profession.

segments.say: Serving your employer is canon three. Protecting society is canon one... and the higher canon always wins. So you don't hide it.
segments.show: Serving your employer is canon 3. Protecting society is canon 1. The higher canon wins, so you don't hide it.

segments.say: Follow for more C I S S P prep.
segments.show: Follow for more CISSP prep.

post.title: Your boss says hide the flaw. What does a CISSP do? #Shorts
post.caption: The CISSP code of ethics has four canons, applied in priority order. Protecting society (canon 1) beats serving your employer (canon 3). Learn the order for exam day.

segments.say: Due care, or due diligence? Most C I S S P candidates mix these up.
segments.show: Due care or due diligence? Most CISSP candidates mix these up.

segments.say: Here's the trick.
segments.show: Here's the trick.

segments.say: Due diligence is doing your homework... researching risks, assessing vendors, writing policies, and checking that controls work.
segments.show: Due diligence is doing your homework: researching risks, assessing vendors, writing policies, checking controls work.

segments.say: Due care is acting on it... putting controls in place, and acting like a reasonable person would. That's the prudent person rule.
segments.show: Due care is acting on it: putting controls in place and acting like a reasonable person would (the prudent person rule).

segments.say: On the exam... investigate, assess, research? Due diligence.
segments.show: On the exam: investigate, assess, research? Due diligence.

segments.say: Implement, maintain, enforce? Due care.
segments.show: Implement, maintain, enforce? Due care.

segments.say: Follow for more C I S S P prep.
segments.show: Follow for more CISSP prep.

post.title: Due care vs due diligence: the 5-second trick #Shorts
post.caption: Due diligence = doing your homework (research, assess, plan). Due care = acting on it (implement, maintain, enforce). A favourite CISSP exam trap.

reels.topic: SLE, ARO and ALE worked example
reels.hook: The one risk formula you must know

segments.say: One formula every C I S S P must know. Let's do it in thirty seconds.
segments.show: One formula every CISSP must know. Let's do it in 30 seconds.

segments.say: A server is worth one hundred thousand dollars.
segments.show: A server is worth $100,000.

segments.say: A flood would destroy forty percent of it. That's the exposure factor.
segments.show: A flood would destroy 40% of it. That's the exposure factor.

segments.say: So the single loss expectancy, S L E, is forty thousand dollars.
segments.show: So the single loss expectancy (SLE) is $40,000.

segments.say: A flood is expected once every ten years. So the annualized rate of occurrence, A R O, is zero point one.
segments.show: A flood is expected once every 10 years, so the annualized rate of occurrence (ARO) is 0.1.

segments.say: Annualized loss expectancy, A L E, equals S L E times A R O... four thousand dollars a year.
segments.show: Annualized loss expectancy (ALE) = SLE × ARO = $4,000 a year.

segments.say: So a safeguard against this flood should never cost more than four thousand dollars a year. Save this one.
segments.show: A safeguard against this flood should never cost more than $4,000 a year. Save this one.

segments.say: Follow for more C I S S P prep.
segments.show: Follow for more CISSP prep.

post.title: SLE × ARO = ALE in 30 seconds (CISSP risk math) #Shorts
post.caption: $100,000 asset × 40% exposure factor = $40,000 SLE. × 0.1 ARO = $4,000 ALE. Never spend more per year on a safeguard than the annual loss it prevents.

segments.say: Quick C I S S P question. Which security document is optional?
segments.show: Quick CISSP question. Which security document is optional?

segments.say: A, policy. B, standard. C, procedure. Or D, guideline. Lock in your answer.
segments.show: A) Policy  B) Standard  C) Procedure  D) Guideline. Lock in your answer.

segments.say: It's D... guideline. Guidelines are recommendations. Everything else is mandatory.
segments.show: It's D, guideline. Guidelines are recommendations. Everything else is mandatory.

segments.say: Policies set direction, and senior management approves them.
segments.show: Policies set direction, and senior management approves them.

segments.say: Standards name exact technologies, like T L S one point two or higher.
segments.show: Standards name exact technologies, like TLS 1.2 or higher.

segments.say: Procedures are step-by-step instructions.
segments.show: Procedures are step-by-step instructions.

segments.say: Follow for more C I S S P prep.
segments.show: Follow for more CISSP prep.

post.title: Which security document is optional? CISSP quiz #Shorts
post.caption: Policy, standard, procedure or guideline? Only guidelines are optional. Policies set direction, standards are specific, procedures are step by step.

segments.say: Six letters that make you think like an attacker. Stride... a threat model from Microsoft.
segments.show: Six letters that make you think like an attacker: STRIDE, a threat model from Microsoft.

segments.say: S, spoofing... pretending to be someone else.
segments.show: S: Spoofing, pretending to be someone else.

segments.say: T, tampering... changing data without permission.
segments.show: T: Tampering, changing data without permission.

segments.say: R, repudiation... denying you did something.
segments.show: R: Repudiation, denying you did something.

segments.say: I, information disclosure... exposing data.
segments.show: I: Information disclosure, exposing data.

segments.say: D, denial of service... blocking access.
segments.show: D: Denial of service, blocking access.

segments.say: E, elevation of privilege... getting more rights than you should.
segments.show: E: Elevation of privilege, getting more rights than you should.

segments.say: Exam tip... threat model early, during design. That's when fixes are cheapest.
segments.show: Exam tip: threat model early, during design. That's when fixes are cheapest.

segments.say: Follow for more C I S S P prep.
segments.show: Follow for more CISSP prep.

post.title: STRIDE threat modeling in 40 seconds #Shorts
post.caption: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege. Each one breaks a security goal. Threat model early, during design.

reels.hook: Can a firewall stop insider fraud?

segments.say: Myth... a firewall stops insider fraud.
segments.show: Myth: a firewall stops insider fraud.

segments.say: Fact... people controls do. Here are three the C I S S P exam loves.
segments.show: Fact: people controls do. Here are three the CISSP exam loves.

segments.say: Separation of duties splits a critical task across two or more people... so fraud needs collusion.
segments.show: Separation of duties splits a critical task across two or more people, so fraud needs collusion.

segments.say: Job rotation moves people between roles... which exposes hidden fraud.
segments.show: Job rotation moves people between roles, which exposes hidden fraud.

segments.say: Mandatory vacations make someone step away... while another person does their job.
segments.show: Mandatory vacations make someone step away while another person does their job.

segments.say: Exam tip... when someone is terminated, disable their access at the same time they're told.
segments.show: Exam tip: when someone is terminated, disable their access at the same time they're told.

segments.say: Follow for more C I S S P prep.
segments.show: Follow for more CISSP prep.

post.title: 3 controls that stop insider fraud (CISSP) #Shorts
post.caption: Separation of duties, job rotation and mandatory vacations. People controls catch what firewalls can't. Bonus: disable access at the moment of termination.

segments.say: M T D, R T O, R P O... three acronyms, one simple rule.
segments.show: MTD, RTO, RPO. Three acronyms, one simple rule.

segments.say: Maximum tolerable downtime, M T D, is the longest the business can survive without a process.
segments.show: Maximum tolerable downtime (MTD): the longest the business can survive without a process.

segments.say: Recovery time objective, R T O, is how fast you plan to bring it back.
segments.show: Recovery time objective (RTO): how fast you plan to bring it back.

segments.say: Recovery point objective, R P O, is how much data you can afford to lose... measured in time since the last good backup.
segments.show: Recovery point objective (RPO): how much data you can afford to lose, measured in time since the last good backup.

segments.say: The rule? R T O must always be shorter than M T D.
segments.show: The rule: RTO must always be shorter than MTD.

segments.say: And in every continuity plan... human safety comes first.
segments.show: And in every continuity plan, human safety comes first.

segments.say: Follow for more C I S S P prep.
segments.show: Follow for more CISSP prep.

post.title: MTD vs RTO vs RPO, explained in 30 seconds #Shorts
post.caption: MTD = longest the business survives without a process. RTO = how fast you restore it. RPO = how much data you can lose. Rule: RTO must be shorter than MTD.

quiz.question: Which risk response is never acceptable?

segments.say: Which of these is never an acceptable risk response?
segments.show: Which of these is never an acceptable risk response?

segments.say: A, mitigate. B, transfer. C, accept. Or D, ignore. Lock in your answer.
segments.show: A) Mitigate  B) Transfer  C) Accept  D) Ignore. Lock in your answer.

segments.say: It's D... ignore. Ignoring a risk is called rejection... and it's never acceptable.
segments.show: It's D, ignore. Ignoring a risk is called rejection, and it's never acceptable.

segments.say: Acceptance is fine... but management must formally agree to it.
segments.show: Acceptance is fine, but management must formally agree to it.

segments.say: And watch this trap. Cyber insurance transfers the cost... not the accountability.
segments.show: Watch this trap: cyber insurance transfers the cost, not the accountability.

segments.say: Follow for more C I S S P prep.
segments.show: Follow for more CISSP prep.

post.title: The one risk response that's never acceptable #Shorts
post.caption: Mitigate, transfer, deter, avoid or accept, but never ignore (rejection). And remember: insurance transfers the cost, not the accountability.

reels.hook: Why not patent the secret recipe?

segments.say: Why would a company never patent its most valuable recipe?
segments.show: Why would a company never patent its most valuable recipe?

segments.say: Because patents expire. A patent protects an invention for twenty years from filing... then anyone can use it.
segments.show: Because patents expire. A patent protects an invention for 20 years from filing. Then anyone can use it.

segments.say: A trade secret needs no registration... and lasts as long as the secret is kept.
segments.show: A trade secret needs no registration, and lasts as long as the secret is kept.

segments.say: Copyright protects original works, like software code... and it's automatic.
segments.show: Copyright protects original works, like software code, and it's automatic.

segments.say: Trademarks protect names and logos. A U S registration lasts ten years... and can be renewed again and again.
segments.show: Trademarks protect names and logos. A US registration lasts 10 years and can be renewed again and again.

segments.say: Exam tip... once a trade secret is disclosed, the protection is gone.
segments.show: Exam tip: once a trade secret is disclosed, the protection is gone.

segments.say: Follow for more C I S S P prep.
segments.show: Follow for more CISSP prep.

post.title: Why companies keep recipes secret instead of patenting #Shorts
post.caption: Patent: 20 years, then public. Trade secret: no registration, lasts while it stays secret. Copyright: automatic. Trademark: 10-year US registration, renewable.

reels.hook: Prove they can't deny sending it

quiz.question: How do you prove a sender can't deny sending a message?

segments.say: Exam question. How do you prove a sender can't deny sending a message?
segments.show: Exam question: how do you prove a sender can't deny sending a message?

segments.say: A, encryption. B, hashing. C, access control. Or D, a digital signature. Lock in your answer.
segments.show: A) Encryption  B) Hashing  C) Access control  D) Digital signature. Lock in your answer.

segments.say: It's D... a digital signature, combined with strong authentication. That's nonrepudiation.
segments.show: It's D: a digital signature, combined with strong authentication. That's nonrepudiation.

segments.say: The C I A triad is confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
segments.show: The CIA triad: confidentiality, integrity and availability.

segments.say: The current exam outline adds authenticity and nonrepudiation... five pillars in total.
segments.show: The current exam outline adds authenticity and nonrepudiation: five pillars in total.

segments.say: Follow for more C I S S P prep.
segments.show: Follow for more CISSP prep.

post.title: Can they deny sending it? CISSP quiz #Shorts
post.caption: Nonrepudiation = proof someone can't deny an action, usually a digital signature with strong authentication. The current exam outline lists five pillars: CIA + authenticity + nonrepudiation.
